description: Opens a three.js, React Three Fiber or WebGL page (a game, viewer, configurator, simulation or shader demo) in headless Chrome (or the `browser` given) on a paused, seeded clock, closing any page already open under the same `game` name, and lists the asset files (models, textures, sounds) it fetched and any fetch that failed, what a dev-server `command` printed as an error or warning, a canvas with no height, and the page's text outside the canvas. Open once: after an edit, the next `interact`, `look`, `observe`, `eval` or `feel` reloads the page by itself. Use it when such a page has been written or changed. Give a file or folder to serve (`url`, relative to cwd), an http URL, or a dev-server `command` run in cwd. Up to 4 games can be open at once, each under its own `game` name: a subagent opens its own (`game: "tester"`) and passes that name to every call.

browser.description: The browser engine the page runs in, chrome by default. firefox is Firefox. Every tool works in each; network (here and in `perf`), `perf`'s throttle and its main-thread time are chrome only.

command.description: A dev-server command run in cwd, as `npx vite --port 0`; the first localhost URL it prints is the page. Closing or reopening this game stops it; an `open` with a url on its origin restarts it on that url.

dpr.description: Device pixel ratio, 1 by default. `look` boxes stay in CSS pixels.

game.description: The name the game was opened under with the `open` tool, to act on ("main" by default; a subagent uses its own).

network.description: Also time a first visit on this network (Chrome DevTools' presets), in real time with no cache: when the first scene frame came, which bytes came before it by kind (as sent: the harness's own server does not compress, a CDN does) and when an overlay over the canvas went.

reducedMotion.description: The page gets prefers-reduced-motion: reduce; `look` then says how much of the picture changed since the last look.

size.description: The page's width and height in CSS pixels until the next open, 1280 × 800 by default, as [1920, 1080].

url.description: A file or folder to serve (relative to cwd), an http URL, or, with `command`, the path and query to open on the server it starts (its origin is the one the command prints).

name: open
